trust_decision.summary: Whether client-supplied bytes may be stored on the daemon as a playable sound file: at the pinned commit the REST upload writes any content under any extension with no type, content or size check.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the media sounds upload; upload_sound is the only UploadFile route in the daemon and writes file.read() straight to /tmp/reachy_mini_sounds/<name>.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST /api/media/sounds/upload (extension allow-list, chunked temp write, content probe, atomic replace; fix.diff:335-369)
HTTP POST /api/media/sounds/upload (new ALLOWED_SOUND_EXTENSIONS frozenset and MAX_SOUND_UPLOAD_BYTES; fix.diff:309-315)
public helper is_valid_audio_file / audio_duration_seconds added after get_sample (fix.diff:394-442), called from the upload route
fix_sites.module_kind: media library (GStreamer pbutils discoverer), separate package

fix_sites.entry_point: create_app middleware stack; MaxBodySizeMiddleware registered for /api/media/sounds/upload (fix.diff:164-168)
new src/reachy_mini/daemon/app/middleware.py MaxBodySizeMiddleware (Content-Length and streamed-body cap), reached via any HTTP request to the listed path

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/reachy_mini/daemon/backend/abstract.py:1575-1597 (upload_audio_start/chunk/finish over WebSocket /ws/sdk and the WebRTC data channel; base64-decoded bytes written to <tempdir>/reachy-mini-uploads/audio/{upload_id}.wav without any content or type check); not touched by the fix

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The command-protocol audio upload is a different feature (move-recording audio over WebRTC/WebSocket), the daemon chooses the .wav name itself, and the advisory only names the REST sounds upload, so a solver can argue it is a separate transport that never accepts a dangerous file type.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-WAV audio (OGG, MP3, FLAC, M4A...) must still upload and play, and a traversal-prefixed name must still be stored as its basename (fix test expects 200); a WAV-only/RIFF-magic or reject-on-slash fix breaks these. The protocol upload likewise documents any GStreamer-decodable container under a .wav name.

O6_input_shapes: allowed extension with non-audio content (evil.wav script)
oversized body via chunked/understated Content-Length (streamed count)
traversal prefix in filename reduced to basename

O7_producer.where: src/reachy_mini/daemon/backend/abstract.py:1575-1597 (protocol audio-upload finish writes the stored file; schema at src/reachy_mini/io/protocol.py:488-548)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebSocket /ws/sdk upload_audio_* commands -> Backend.process_command -> _handle_audio_finish writes arbitrary decoded bytes to disk with no content validation
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different transport and feature (motion-recording audio); file name is forced to {upload_id}.wav so 'no dangerous type' seems to hold.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: io/ and daemon/backend/ packages, 3 files from routers/media.py

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebRTC data-channel upload_audio_* commands -> _handle_webrtc_message -> process_command -> same unvalidated write
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Peer-to-peer media transport, looks unrelated to the HTTP API named in the report.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: daemon/backend/abstract.py, a ~2000-line file in another package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A play_sound variant accepting a URL/base64 payload that it saves into SOUNDS_TMP_DIR before playback
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: play_sound already resolves names against SOUNDS_TMP_DIR; a one-shot 'upload and play' convenience is a natural addition for WebRTC clients.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Move upload finish writing an attached sound blob (from the move JSON) to disk next to the move
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Move and audio slots already share upload_id; embedding audio in the move payload is a plausible simplification.

O9_family: CWE-434 unrestricted upload of dangerous file type (content/type validation of stored uploads)

O10_build.toolchain: pip/uv from pyproject.toml; PyGObject + system GStreamer (gst-plugins incl. pbutils) on Linux
O10_build.project_tests: pytest; no tests for the upload routes at the pinned commit (tests/unit_tests/test_media_backend.py, test_media_server_watchdog.py cover other media code); fix adds tests/unit_tests/test_media_upload_api.py using FastAPI TestClient with gst-gated cases

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an extension allow-list (or .wav-only check) to upload_sound and stop, leaving content unvalidated and the protocol audio upload untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: upload_id is an unvalidated client string joined into the audio temp path (src/reachy_mini/daemon/backend/abstract.py:1595), a path-traversal concern separate from CWE-434.
play_sound accepts absolute daemon paths (src/reachy_mini/daemon/app/routers/media.py:64-81); arbitrary-file read into GStreamer, not this advisory.
unverified: Whether the WebRTC/WS routes are reachable without auth in the default daemon config (loopback binding off-wireless per commit 2cd35b18) was not checked.
Whether the latest release still lacks validation on the protocol audio upload: no latest tree given.
Content-validation tests need system GStreamer with pbutils in the image; not confirmed buildable offline.
